state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: The negative-sloping section on the distance-time graph represents Fido moving away from his home. Remember, when the line slopes downwards, it means the distance is increasing in the opposite direction. Make sure to pay attention to the direction of the line to determine whether Fido is moving closer or further away from home.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Oh right, so when the line goes down it means he's moving away? But I'm confused because I thought if the line goes down that means the distance is getting smaller... like, shouldn't that mean he's coming back home closer to where he started?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: When the line on a distance-time graph slopes downwards, it means that the distance is increasing in the opposite direction, away from the starting point. Remember, the direction of the line indicates the direction of movement, not the actual distance. So, in this case, Fido is moving further away from home during the negative-sloping section.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Wait, I'm still confused though... if the line goes down on the graph, doesn't that mean the number on the y-axis is getting smaller? Like, if it starts at 10 metres and goes down to 5 metres, isn't Fido closer to home, not further away?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher repeatedly provides mathematically incorrect information (claiming downward slopes mean moving away when they actually mean returning home), fails to engage with the student's correct reasoning in Turn 4, and the student becomes increasingly confused rather than improving.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher provides incorrect information and fails to give direct corrective feedback on the student's correct reasoning, which contradicts the rule-based strategy of stating explicit procedures and giving direct corrective feedback on errors.
